name: Meshell Ndegeocello
notes: The lane's bassist-auteur, "credited with helping spark the neo-soul movement". Every number here is subordinated to the entry's central claim: "bass is the lead voice and the compositional engine… thumb-and-finger funk 16ths, wide register (E1 to above C4), slides, harmonics, chordal double-stops, and long unaccompanied bass statements". So the bassline carries the lowest root probability and the widest register in the whole section — up to 54, which forced the chord voicing to start at 56 so the generated keys stay above it — with a real glide probability for the slides. The kit is the inverse: "sparse, dry and low — kick on 1 and 3½, snare or rim on 2&4 but quiet, hats minimal", so `secondaryAnchor` is 3&, the velocity tiers are the quietest in this batch, the hat is non-continuous at a fill density of 0.12, and the ghost probability is near zero. Harmony is "long dorian/aeolian vamps, quartal keyboard voicings" with "few and slow" chord changes, which is `maxChords` 2, a vamp-weighted harmonic rhythm and chord durations of 8–16 beats. Vocals are "low-alto, half-spoken, androgynous in placement, with very low note-density and long rests" — the lowest register and density here plus a high `emptyBarBias`. ⚠ The INFERRED parameters are all drum numbers, the melody figures and the bass probabilities; the research marks tempo and drum parameters as inference and [LOW-CONF]. ⚠ The reggae one-drop variant the entry names is real but is not encoded — this model states the straight 2&4 spine only. ⚠ **`chords.harmonicRhythm` re-weighted (2026-08-17, harmony variety floor).** The entry's harmony line is "long dorian/aeolian vamps, quartal keyboard voicings, and lead-sheet-derived harmony ... Chord changes are few and slow", and the engine's `vamp` value is *one* chord held for the whole clip (`generators::chords`: "One chord for the whole pattern") — so a `vamp`-dominant weighting rendered a **one**-chord bed the research nowhere describes. The changes now happen at `2_bars_per_chord`, with `vamp` as the minority. "Few and slow" is why `1_per_bar` is not authored — and "chord changes" is why a single 4-bar hold cannot be the usual case. ⚠ **The countermelody reached 876/1000 distinct answers against a floor of 980 (2026-08-17, counter variety floor).** `melody.emptyBarBias` came down from 0.3 to 0.1. The counter's note count is `densityRatio` times the lead's own note count, so a bar the lead leaves empty is a bar the counter has nothing to answer — and one empty region is IDENTICAL to every other one, which is the single thing a seed cannot vary. Measured across this roster the models failing this gate average 0.150 here against 0.030 for the models that pass. Second, `melody.densityPerBar` went from [1, 4] to [2, 5]. A lead allowed to thin to a single note a bar leaves the counter almost nothing to answer, and no amount of counter density recovers what the lead never played. This is the lead becoming reliably present rather than busier — the floor is what moved and the ceiling carries the density claim. Third, `countermelody.densityRatio` became a range, [0.28, 0.45], rather than a flat 0.28. That parameter decides how many notes the part has at all, and at 0.28 it was two or three; a part that short has almost no shapes to be distinct in. The low end is kept because it is the thin reading the entry's texture implies, and it is now the bottom of a band rather than the only answer — so how much of the lead the pad answers varies take to take. ⚠ Every value that moved here is INFERRED rather than a researched claim — the entry's Melody/chords line reads "Rhodes/organ pads, distorted guitar, muted trumpet; the harmonic bed is often just bass plus one sustained keyboard voice. Vocals are low-alto, half-spoken, androgynous in placement, with very low note-density and long rests.", and every claim in it still holds after the change.
